lines.text: Today you mix chance with functions, roll hundreds of dice in a blink and build a Ludo race.

Your game code starts to read like a story.

Counting the results shows patterns, like a six coming up about one time in six.
Scientists and game designers test ideas this way.
def take_turn(name, position): handles one player’s whole turn.
It rolls, moves, prints and returns the new position.
Two players simply call it with different names.
Game rules can be functions too. move(position, roll) returns the square you land on, and keeps you still if you would go past the finish.
Small rule functions are easy to test.
The parameter sides decides how big the dice is.

The loop rolls the dice six hundred times faster than you can blink.
We get close to one hundred sixes, about one roll in every six.
From square ten, a four takes you to square fourteen.
From square twenty-eight, a five would pass the finish at thirty, so you stay where you are.
